tasks.short: Supervise histology benches and resolve the day's work constraints

steps.what: Review pending histology cases and bench status
Supervise tissue processing and safe bench practice
Resolve histology priorities and instruct bench staff
Update the existing histology bench assignment board

tasks.design: Configure the existing histology laboratory system in {OTHER} to retain the supervisor's queue filters and reuse case identifiers on its existing bench assignment board. Only navigation and repeated identifier entry shrink; bench observation, prioritisation, instructions and ordinary board saves retain their time.
tasks.previous_blocker: Status screens and assignment entries require repeated navigation and case identification.
tasks.enabler_now: Native queue filters and case-linked board fields may already support these operations.
tasks.still_hard: A delayed fixation, urgent specimen or inexperienced operator needs direct technical judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The supervisor sees unsafe practice and negotiates feasible priorities at the bench.
tasks.altitude: The supervisor retains the same technical and staffing decisions.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: laboratory systems can expose case queues and link assignments to existing case identifiers; this is a capability hypothesis, not a measured histology saving.

assumptions: Boundary is day-to-day histology bench supervision with an already-used electronic bench board, not laboratory management in full. Staff use that board to find their assigned cases; no new supervision log is proposed. A laboratory without this board needs a different graph and time weighting.

The accessioning staff already produce case identifier, specimen type and requested examination; bench staff maintain processing stage and responsible bench in their normal work. s1 includes checking completeness and manually tracing missing status. No new staff capture is free or transferred.

Test native saved filters and case-linked assignment fields first. The three points removed from s1 are screen navigation only, leaving 17 points to inspect status and trace exceptions. The 1.5 points removed from s4 are repeated case identifier entry; assignment judgement, field checks, missing-case entry and ordinary save remain in its 13.5 points.

Instructions in s3 are live internal supervision. s4 is the author's ordinary internal board update and needs no self-approval stage. No new automatic dispatch or diagnostic release is proposed. Actual separate escalation reports or sends, if required locally, need their own timed actions.
Shares and upkeep are provisional model estimates, not observed organisation baselines. Existing system runtime earns no labour saving.
unknowns: Whether a case-linked board is used today and how much repeated navigation exists
Who maintains stage status and how often it is stale
research_questions: Observe a supervision shift and time navigation separately from clinical interpretation
Can native board fields avoid identifier re-entry without concealing missing status?

already_counted.description: Inspect status, trace missing data and check board assignments; ordinary save remains included.

incremental.description: Maintain queue filters and verify board field mappings after laboratory workflow changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central removes 3 navigation points and 1.5 identifier-entry points, less 0.8 upkeep. Conservative mixed-stage handover: only 1 point of navigation and 0.4 points of identifiers are reusable; manual status tracing and board entry retain the rest, giving 1.4 minus 0.8 = 0.6.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Teach students and staff histology methods

steps.what: Choose histology teaching examples and prepare technical content
Lay out existing histology teaching handout content
Check handout meaning and prepare physical teaching materials
Demonstrate histology techniques to students or staff
Observe learner practice and give technical feedback

tasks.design: Use a native {DOCS} handout template for the headings and layout of teaching material already prepared today. The histotechnologist chooses examples, checks every instruction against the validated procedure, then demonstrates and coaches directly.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated handout formatting consumes a small part of preparation.
tasks.enabler_now: An existing document template can apply headings and layout without generating clinical instructions.
tasks.still_hard: Learners need correction of physical technique and explanation adapted to their mistakes.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher recognises a learner's misunderstanding and intervenes safely during practice.
tasks.altitude: The teacher spends slightly less preparation time formatting, with unchanged teaching authority.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native document templates can apply fixed teaching handout layouts while people retain technical authorship and checking.

assumptions: Boundary is a practical lesson for which the teacher already prepares a handout that learners use during demonstration. If teaching is entirely oral without a handout, remove its preparation and layout shares and reweight; do not create paperwork to justify savings.

s1 produces the selected procedure revision, learning objectives, teacher-written instruction text and permitted examples from existing validated procedures. s2 accepts that complete content; absent or incompatible content is laid out manually within s3's retained checking and preparation allowance.

Try native document styles before code. The five points in s2 represent repeated headings and spacing, not original lesson design, ordinary saving, printing or a send. s3 retains all content checking, minor layout repair and physical preparation; if substantial repair exceeds this allowance, reduce the estimate.

No formal competency certificate, pupil record or separate material dispatch is established by this teaching task. If required in practice, count the actual assessment, record entry and each dispatch separately. Do not invent a trailing attendance log.
All shares are provisional model estimates. Learner practice time is outside the focal teacher's denominator; s5 is the teacher's observation and feedback time.
unknowns: Which lessons actually use repeatable handouts
How often tissue images or accessibility requirements require manual layout
research_questions: Compare handout formatting and technical preparation separately for a recurring staining lesson
Does the native template preserve warnings, image captions and procedure revisions?

already_counted.description: Full technical instruction check, minor layout repair and preparation of physical teaching materials.

incremental.description: Maintain the teaching handout layout as validated procedure presentation requirements change.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central removes five points of existing layout work, less 0.5 upkeep. Conservative one-off stain demonstration needs custom image placement and warnings, leaving only one point of fixed headings reusable: 1 minus 0.5 = 0.5. Teaching and technical authorship never shrink.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: A bench supervisor and practical teacher with slightly less navigation and document layout work.
skills_to_grow: Configure case-linked queue views without hiding exceptions
Maintain teaching templates against validated procedure revisions
role.ambitious_version: Keep direct supervision and hands-on teaching central while reducing demonstrable repeated screen and formatting work.
